# Commands

Every command in QuakeC Studio's command registry (PRIN-3): the one list behind the menus, keystrokes, command palette, CLI, agent tools and MCP tools. Each command has a stable id and takes one JSON object as its parameters, described by the JSON Schema (2020-12) below. Commands that change state can be undone with `edit.undo`.

| Command | Summary |
| --- | --- |
| [`checkpoint.create`](#checkpointcreate) | Records every file of the open project, as it is on disk, as a checkpoint to restore, in a git store of its own. |
| [`checkpoint.list`](#checkpointlist) | Lists the open project's checkpoints, oldest first. |
| [`checkpoint.restore`](#checkpointrestore) | Puts every file of the open project back as a checkpoint holds it, removing the files made since and dropping unsaved edits. |
| [`code.actions`](#codeactions) | Lists the quick fixes for the diagnostics at a place in a file: a missing builtin declared, a misspelled field corrected, an unused local removed, a missing precache added. |
| [`code.fix`](#codefix) | Applies a quick fix for the diagnostics at a place in a file, the first unless one is named by its index in code.actions' list; the file is not saved. |
| [`commands.list`](#commandslist) | Lists every command with its id, summary and parameter schema. |
| [`compile`](#compile) | Compiles the open project and says whether it is clean, with its error counts. |
| [`edit.accept`](#editaccept) | Accepts staged hunks: their lines stay in the editor's text, unsaved, once each hunk of their file is decided. |
| [`edit.apply`](#editapply) | Stages a change to several files as hunks to accept or reject one by one; the project is checked with them, and nothing is written to disk. |
| [`edit.redo`](#editredo) | Makes the most recently undone change again. |
| [`edit.reject`](#editreject) | Rejects staged hunks: the lines they replaced come back, byte for byte. |
| [`edit.staged`](#editstaged) | Lists the staged hunks waiting to be accepted or rejected. |
| [`edit.undo`](#editundo) | Takes back the most recent change that has not been undone. |
| [`editor.fold`](#editorfold) | Folds the innermost block or block comment at the caret. |
| [`editor.fold_all`](#editorfold_all) | Folds every block and block comment of the open file, each down to its first and last lines. |
| [`editor.go_to_line`](#editorgo_to_line) | Moves the caret to a line of the open file, from 1; without a line it asks for one. |
| [`editor.go_to_symbol`](#editorgo_to_symbol) | Opens a picker of the open file's symbols, to move the caret to one. |
| [`editor.toggle_soft_wrap`](#editortoggle_soft_wrap) | Turns soft wrap on or off: long lines wrap at the editor's width. |
| [`editor.unfold`](#editorunfold) | Unfolds the innermost folded block or comment at the caret. |
| [`editor.unfold_all`](#editorunfold_all) | Unfolds every folded block and block comment of the open file, showing all of its lines. |
| [`engine.builtins`](#enginebuiltins) | Lists an engine's builtins for a module kind, each with its number or engine name, QuakeC name, signature and extensions; the open project's engine and server QuakeC when none is named. |
| [`engine.console`](#engineconsole) | Runs a command in the running game's console and answers the lines it printed. |
| [`engine.inspect`](#engineinspect) | Reads the running game: the edicts in use, one edict's fields, every named global, or the call stack while stopped in a frame. |
| [`engine.screenshot`](#enginescreenshot) | Writes the frame the running game draws as a PNG, in the project's build/screenshots unless a path is given, and answers where and its size. |
| [`file.close`](#fileclose) | Closes a file's tab, opening the tab beside it when it was         the open file; its unsaved text is kept. |
| [`file.format`](#fileformat) | Formats a QuakeC file: each line indented with tabs to its depth, trailing white space removed. Only white space at the ends of lines changes, so it compiles to the same progs.dat; the file is not saved. |
| [`file.inlay_hints`](#fileinlay_hints) | Lists a file's inlay hints: the name of the parameter each argument of a call is passed as. |
| [`file.open`](#fileopen) | Opens a file in the editor, with the caret at a byte offset or at the start. |
| [`file.read`](#fileread) | Reads a file's current text: the editor's when it has unsaved changes, else what is on disk. |
| [`file.replace_all`](#filereplace_all) | Replaces every match of a search in a file and saves it, as one undoable change; matching case, whole words and regular expressions as project.search. |
| [`file.replace_range`](#filereplace_range) | Replaces a byte range of a file's text, in the editor's text; nothing is saved. An edit in an excerpt of the multibuffer. |
| [`file.save`](#filesave) | Writes a file's current text, as the editor has it, to disk. |
| [`file.update`](#fileupdate) | Takes the whole text of a file as an editor has it, unsaved, and checks the project again. |
| [`files.changed`](#fileschanged) | Takes files another program changed: the open map is read again when it has no unsaved edits, else kept for map.resolve; changed QuakeC is read again with the entity definitions derived from it. |
| [`git.blame`](#gitblame) | Says who last changed each line of a file, and in which commit. |
| [`git.branches`](#gitbranches) | Lists the repository's local branches, the checked-out one marked. |
| [`git.commit`](#gitcommit) | Commits what is staged with a message; the new commit's id. |
| [`git.conflicts`](#gitconflicts) | Lists a file's merge conflicts: where each one's markers are. |
| [`git.create_branch`](#gitcreate_branch) | Creates a branch at the current commit and checks it out, as git switch -c does. |
| [`git.diff`](#gitdiff) | Lists the hunks of a file's unstaged or staged changes. |
| [`git.head_text`](#githead_text) | Gives a file's text at HEAD, which the editor marks its changes against; none for a file HEAD does not have. |
| [`git.log`](#gitlog) | Lists the commits that changed a file, the newest first, following renames. |
| [`git.resolve`](#gitresolve) | Resolves one of a file's merge conflicts by keeping our side, theirs or both, and saves the file. |
| [`git.stage`](#gitstage) | Stages a file, or one hunk of its unstaged changes. |
| [`git.status`](#gitstatus) | Lists the project repository's branch and changed files, staged and not, as git status does; none when the project is not in a git repository. |
| [`git.switch`](#gitswitch) | Checks out a branch, as git switch does, and reads the project's files again; refused while files have unsaved edits. |
| [`git.unstage`](#gitunstage) | Unstages a file, or one hunk of its staged changes. |
| [`map.brush_chamfer`](#mapbrush_chamfer) | Chamfers an edge of a brush into one or more bevel faces, from a distance along each of its two faces (MAP-15.9). |
| [`map.brush_clip`](#mapbrush_clip) | Clips a brush of the open map by the plane through three points, keeping the part behind it, in front of it, or both as two brushes. |
| [`map.brush_create`](#mapbrush_create) | Adds a box brush from two corners, snapped to the grid (16 units unless given), to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture. |
| [`map.brush_delete`](#mapbrush_delete) | Deletes a brush of an entity of the open map. |
| [`map.brush_extrude`](#mapbrush_extrude) | Moves a face of a brush along its normal by a distance snapped to the grid, out or in, its texture fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.3). |
| [`map.brush_hollow`](#mapbrush_hollow) | Hollows a brush into walls of a thickness: the brush becomes itself with the brush its walls enclose taken out (MAP-15.5). |
| [`map.brush_intersect`](#mapbrush_intersect) | Replaces two or more brushes of an entity with the solid all of them hold, which takes the first's place (MAP-15.6). |
| [`map.brush_merge`](#mapbrush_merge) | Merges two or more brushes of an entity of the open map into their convex hull, which takes the first's place. |
| [`map.brush_move`](#mapbrush_move) | Moves brushes of an entity by an offset snapped to the grid (16 units unless given), their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free. |
| [`map.brush_scale`](#mapbrush_scale) | Scales brushes of an entity by factors along x, y and z about a point, the middle of their bounds unless given, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2). |
| [`map.brush_shape`](#mapbrush_shape) | Adds a shape of brushes filling a box, its corners snapped to the grid: a cylinder (solid or hollow), cone, arch, UV or icosahedron spheroid, rock, scalable curve of 12, 24, 48 or 96 sides, or straight or spiral stairs whose default step a player climbs; to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture. |
| [`map.brush_shear`](#mapbrush_shear) | Shears brushes of an entity: each point moves along one axis by a factor times its distance from a point along another, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2). |
| [`map.brush_split_edge`](#mapbrush_split_edge) | Splits an edge of a brush by a new vertex at a point snapped to the grid, or a distance out from the edge's middle (MAP-15.8). |
| [`map.brush_split_face`](#mapbrush_split_face) | Splits a face of a brush by a new vertex in front of it, at a point snapped to the grid, or a distance out from the face's middle (MAP-15.8). |
| [`map.brush_subtract`](#mapbrush_subtract) | Subtracts a brush of the open map from every other brush of its entity, then deletes it: the brushes it overlapped become the parts outside it. |
| [`map.brush_sweep`](#mapbrush_sweep) | Sweeps a brush along a path of points snapped to the grid: the brush becomes one brush for each step, the hull of it at the step's two ends (MAP-15.4). |
| [`map.brush_texture`](#mapbrush_texture) | Sets the texture, shift, rotation or scale of every face of brushes of an entity, keeping what is not given (MAP-12). |
| [`map.brush_vertex`](#mapbrush_vertex) | Moves a vertex of a brush of the open map to a point snapped to the grid; the brush becomes the convex hull of its vertices so moved. |
| [`map.brush_vertices`](#mapbrush_vertices) | Moves several vertices of a brush at once, each to a point snapped to the grid; the brush becomes the hull of its vertices so moved (MAP-15.7). |
| [`map.check`](#mapcheck) | Checks a .map: what id's qbsp and ericw-tools read otherwise, and its entities against the project's server QuakeC as the engine reads them: unknown classnames and keys with the closest name, values their field cannot read, and targets and targetnames nothing matches. |
| [`map.compare`](#mapcompare) | How the open map's file, changed by another program, differs from the map being edited, entity by entity. |
| [`map.compile`](#mapcompile) | Compiles the open map, as it is in the editor, to a BSP beside it, with its portal and leak files, and reports whether it leaks and the textures its WADs lack. |
| [`map.delete`](#mapdelete) | Deletes an entity of the open map; the world stays. |
| [`map.duplicate`](#mapduplicate) | Duplicates an entity of the open map, its keys and brushes, in place at the end of the map, and selects the copy; the world is not duplicated. A targetname ending in a number takes the next free number, and the keys the code fires entities by move on by as many. |
| [`map.entity`](#mapentity) | An entity of the open map: its pairs, the keys its class reads with their types and defaults, and the map's targetnames for its target keys. |
| [`map.export`](#mapexport) | Writes the open map to another .map without the layers marked to be left out of exports and the entities in them (TrenchBroom's Export). |
| [`map.face_align`](#mapface_align) | Carries one face's texture alignment onto other faces of the open map, so the texture continues across the line their planes share (MAP-13.8). |
| [`map.face_uv`](#mapface_uv) | Fits, justifies, flips, resets, snaps or adjusts the texture of faces of the open map, at the size its WAD gives it (MAP-13). |
| [`map.filter`](#mapfilter) | The entities of the open map the game removes at a skill and in a kind of game (single, coop or deathmatch), found by spawning the map with the project's program: those the spawnflags rule out and those the QuakeC removes. |
| [`map.fix`](#mapfix) | Applies a quick fix `map.issues` gave, as one step with undo. |
| [`map.hide`](#maphide) | Hides entities of the open map in the editor until map.show_all (TrenchBroom's Hide Selection); the map is not changed. |
| [`map.inspect`](#mapinspect) | The open map's rooms (TrenchBroom's named layers and groups, with their bounds) and its entities: each one's place, classname, origin, targetname and room, filtered by room or classname. |
| [`map.isolate`](#mapisolate) | Hides every entity of the open map but these in the editor until map.show_all (TrenchBroom's Isolate Selection); the map is not changed. |
| [`map.issues`](#mapissues) | Lists every issue of the open map, each with the entity or brush it is about and a quick fix where one exists: its format's, brushes with no volume, a missing player start, missing textures and, with a project open, its entities' against the server QuakeC. |
| [`map.layers`](#maplayers) | The open map's TrenchBroom layers: each one's name, whether it is hidden, locked or left out of exports, and how many entities are in it. |
| [`map.leaks`](#mapleaks) | Compiles the open map in memory and reports whether it leaks, with the trail from the entity the outside reaches out to the void, and the textures its WADs lack. |
| [`map.link`](#maplink) | Points a key of an entity of the open map, one the code fires entities by such as target or killtarget, at another entity: the key takes the other's targetname, and the other its classname and the next free number as one when it has none. |
| [`map.lock`](#maplock) | Locks entities of the open map against edits until map.unlock_all; the map is not changed. |
| [`map.move`](#mapmove) | Moves an entity of the open map: a point entity's origin, a brush entity's brushes. |
| [`map.move_to`](#mapmove_to) | Moves an entity or a group of the open map into a layer or a group, or into the default layer given the world, as TrenchBroom writes it. |
| [`map.open`](#mapopen) | Opens a .map in the map view, or a shipped .bsp's entities when the map has no .map source; nothing is selected. |
| [`map.outline`](#mapoutline) | The open map's outline: the default layer and each layer, their groups and linked groups, then their entities by classname and targetname, with brush counts; with filter, only what holds the text and what is around it. |
| [`map.place`](#mapplace) | Places a point entity of a classname at an origin in the open map, with the keys given, and selects it. |
| [`map.place_prefab`](#mapplace_prefab) | Copies a prefab into the open map with its origin at a point on the grid: its world's brushes into the world, its other entities after the map's. |
| [`map.play_from_here`](#mapplay_from_here) | Compiles the open map fast, with no vis and fast light, into the project's build, starts the game on it and puts the player at a point, facing a way: the map view's camera (MAP-13). |
| [`map.prefabs`](#mapprefabs) | Lists the .map files in the project's prefabs folder. |
| [`map.remove_key`](#mapremove_key) | Removes every pair with a key from an entity of the open map. |
| [`map.rename_key`](#maprename_key) | Renames a key in every open .map, keeping each value and its formatting: what to run once the person confirms, after symbol.rename renames a field a map may name. Nothing is saved. |
| [`map.resolve`](#mapresolve) | After another program changed the open map's file while it had unsaved edits: keep disk to read the file again, or mine to keep the edits and save them over it. |
| [`map.rotate`](#maprotate) | Turns a point entity of the open map about the vertical: its angle, or its angles' yaw. |
| [`map.save`](#mapsave) | Saves the open map: a .map over itself; a BSP's entities as a .ent beside it (bsp: ent, the default) or into the BSP's entity lump (bsp: lump). |
| [`map.save_prefab`](#mapsave_prefab) | Writes brushes of the world and whole entities of the open map as a prefab in the project's prefabs folder, around the middle of their floor. |
| [`map.search`](#mapsearch) | Finds the open map's entities and brushes by classname, key, value, texture and a box, every part given; text matches in any case. |
| [`map.select`](#mapselect) | Selects an entity of the open map, or clears the selection. |
| [`map.set_flag`](#mapset_flag) | Sets or clears one spawnflag of an entity of the open map, and of the entities in also, in one step, keeping each entity's other flags. |
| [`map.set_key`](#mapset_key) | Sets a key of an entity of the open map, and of the entities in also with it in one step: its last occurrence keeps its place and formatting, a new key goes after the others. |
| [`map.set_layer`](#mapset_layer) | Turns a layer of the open map hidden, locked or left out of exports on or off, written as TrenchBroom writes it. |
| [`map.show_all`](#mapshow_all) | Shows every entity of the open map hidden in the editor (TrenchBroom's Show All); a hidden layer stays hidden. |
| [`map.textures`](#maptextures) | Lists the open map's textures: those of the WADs its world names, found in the project, beside the map or in the game, and of the BSP it was opened from, each with its size and how many faces use it, and the names its faces use that nothing holds. |
| [`map.unlock_all`](#mapunlock_all) | Unlocks every entity of the open map locked in the editor; a locked layer stays locked. |
| [`preview.breakpoint`](#previewbreakpoint) | Adds a breakpoint at a line of a file, or takes it away when there is one; set in the running game too and in each game that starts. |
| [`preview.choose_game`](#previewchoose_game) | Chooses the folder the preview reads the game from, in place, and says what it holds; a folder that cannot be played is not kept. |
| [`preview.console`](#previewconsole) | Runs a command in the running game's console. |
| [`preview.dock`](#previewdock) | Docks the game's window beside the IDE's window, given where the IDE's window is and whether it has the focus. |
| [`preview.game`](#previewgame) | Says what game data the preview plays from: the chosen folder, or the first install found, as found, shareware only, rerelease only or missing, with the files it lacks. |
| [`preview.pause`](#previewpause) | Pauses the running game between frames. |
| [`preview.pick`](#previewpick) | Selects the edict under a point of the game's window. |
| [`preview.play`](#previewplay) | Builds the open project and starts the preview host on its program, stopping a game already running. |
| [`preview.poll`](#previewpoll) | Reads the running game's events: its state changes and console lines. |
| [`preview.reload`](#previewreload) | Builds the open project and reloads its program in the running game, the map going on; nothing when no game runs. |
| [`preview.restart`](#previewrestart) | Starts the running game's map again. |
| [`preview.resume`](#previewresume) | Resumes the paused game. |
| [`preview.select`](#previewselect) | Selects an edict of the running game and reads its fields for the Properties panel. |
| [`preview.set_field`](#previewset_field) | Sets a field of the selected edict while the game is paused, the value read as the field's type. |
| [`preview.step`](#previewstep) | Runs one server frame of the game, pausing it first, and leaves it paused. |
| [`preview.step_by`](#previewstep_by) | Steps the game stopped in a frame by a statement, into a call, over one or out to the caller. |
| [`preview.stop`](#previewstop) | Stops the game. |
| [`preview.unwatch`](#previewunwatch) | Takes a watch away. |
| [`preview.watch`](#previewwatch) | Adds a watch, an expression read each time the game stops in a frame. |
| [`project.build`](#projectbuild) | Compiles each module of the open project, with the editor's text of each open file, and writes its progs.dat and .lno. |
| [`project.check`](#projectcheck) | Lists every error and warning in the open project, as the Problems panel does. |
| [`project.entities`](#projectentities) | Lists the entity classes the open project's server QuakeC defines, read from its spawn functions: each class's keys, defaults, spawnflags, comment, model and size; with fgd, also writes them as an FGD file for other map editors. |
| [`project.export`](#projectexport) | Builds the open project and exports it as a zip players install: its programs, its own assets (optionally in pak0.pak), a README and its license notices, never id's game data. |
| [`project.files`](#projectfiles) | Lists every source file the open project compiles, by path. |
| [`project.info`](#projectinfo) | Describes the open project: its directory and each module's kind, dialect, target engine and output. |
| [`project.new`](#projectnew) | Makes a new project from a starter template, id's QuakeC 1.01 or the rerelease's, with quakec.toml, a sample test and the GPLv2 notices; it builds and plays at once. |
| [`project.open`](#projectopen) | Opens the QuakeC project in a directory: its quakec.toml, or its progs.src and csprogs.src. |
| [`project.search`](#projectsearch) | Finds every match of a text in the open project's files, unsaved edits included, by file, line and byte range; matching case, whole words only or as a regular expression. |
| [`project.symbols`](#projectsymbols) | Lists the open project's global definitions, functions, globals and fields, each with where its name is first written; a query keeps those whose name contains it. |
| [`project.take_checked`](#projecttake_checked) | Takes the problems, symbols and highlighting the background check worked out for the latest edit, if it has finished; says whether anything changed. |
| [`project.test`](#projecttest) | Builds the open project and runs its tests: each test_ function called alone in the VM over a mock engine, and each scenario under tests/ played in the server simulation, answering each test's verdict. |
| [`scenario.run`](#scenariorun) | Builds the open project and plays a scenario file on it in the server simulation, answering whether each assertion held, with the values read, and writing its screenshots beside it. |
| [`settings.get`](#settingsget) | Gives one setting's value and where it comes from. |
| [`settings.list`](#settingslist) | Lists every setting with its default, its value and where the value comes from. |
| [`settings.reset`](#settingsreset) | Removes a setting from the user's or the project's settings file and writes the file. |
| [`settings.set`](#settingsset) | Sets a setting in the user's or the project's settings file and writes the file. |
| [`symbol.complete`](#symbolcomplete) | Lists the names that may be written at a place. |
| [`symbol.definition`](#symboldefinition) | Finds where the name at a place is defined. |
| [`symbol.hover`](#symbolhover) | Says what the name at a place is: its declaration and its comment. |
| [`symbol.references`](#symbolreferences) | Finds every declaration and use of the name at a place, in every file. |
| [`symbol.rename`](#symbolrename) | Renames the name at a place everywhere it is written, in the editor's text of each file; nothing is saved. |
| [`task.list`](#tasklist) | Lists the open project's tasks: the named command lines of its quakec.toml. |
| [`task.run`](#taskrun) | Runs one of the open project's tasks in a new terminal tab, by the user's shell in the project directory. |
| [`terminal.close`](#terminalclose) | Closes a terminal tab, ending its process. |
| [`terminal.new`](#terminalnew) | Opens the user's shell in the project directory in a new terminal tab. |
| [`terminal.poll`](#terminalpoll) | Takes what the terminal tabs have written and how their processes ended, without waiting; true when any tab changed. |
| [`terminal.send`](#terminalsend) | Writes a line to a terminal tab's shell. |
| [`texture.import`](#textureimport) | Imports a PNG image as a texture: quantized to the game's palette with its mip levels, written into the project's own WAD in textures/, in place of a texture of the same name, and that WAD named in the open map's world. |
| [`view.close_split`](#viewclose_split) | Closes the editor's second pane. |
| [`view.focus_bottom_panel`](#viewfocus_bottom_panel) | Shows the bottom panel, Problems, Console and the debugger, if it is hidden and gives it the keyboard. |
| [`view.focus_editor`](#viewfocus_editor) | Gives the keyboard to the editor in the centre. |
| [`view.focus_left_panel`](#viewfocus_left_panel) | Shows the left panel, Project and Entities, if it is hidden and gives it the keyboard. |
| [`view.focus_right_panel`](#viewfocus_right_panel) | Shows the right panel, Properties and the agent, if it is hidden and gives it the keyboard. |
| [`view.map_panes`](#viewmap_panes) | Splits the map view: the 3D view alone, with a top view in its corner, or beside top, front and side views. |
| [`view.project_search`](#viewproject_search) | Opens the project search: every match in the project's files as a multibuffer of editable excerpts, to edit or replace in place. |
| [`view.resize_panel`](#viewresize_panel) | Sets the width of the left or right panel, or the height of the bottom panel, in points. |
| [`view.split_down`](#viewsplit_down) | Splits the editor into two panes, one above the other, the second showing the open file. |
| [`view.split_right`](#viewsplit_right) | Splits the editor into two panes side by side, the second showing the open file. |
| [`view.tab_switcher`](#viewtab_switcher) | Opens the tab switcher: the open files, the one used most recently first. |
| [`view.toggle_outline`](#viewtoggle_outline) | Shows or hides the outline panel beside the editor: the open file's symbols, the one the caret is in marked. |
| [`view.toggle_panel`](#viewtoggle_panel) | Shows or hides a panel: Project and Entities on the left, Properties and the agent on the right, or Problems, Console and the debugger at the bottom. |
| [`vm.run`](#vmrun) | Builds the open project and calls one QuakeC function in the VM over a mock engine, with globals and the fields of a self edict set first, answering each global and field the call changed and any run error. |

## `checkpoint.create`

Records every file of the open project, as it is on disk, as a checkpoint to restore, in a git store of its own.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `checkpoint.create`.",
  "properties": {
    "label": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "What the checkpoint is for, such as the agent run's task; `checkpoint` when absent.",
      "type": [
        "string",
        "null"
      ]
    }
  },
  "title": "CreateCheckpointParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `checkpoint.list`

Lists the open project's checkpoints, oldest first.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The command takes no parameters: pass the empty object {}.",
  "title": "No parameters",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `checkpoint.restore`

Puts every file of the open project back as a checkpoint holds it, removing the files made since and dropping unsaved edits.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "CheckpointNumber": {
      "description": "A checkpoint's number, which `checkpoint.restore` takes.",
      "format": "uint32",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `checkpoint.restore`.",
  "properties": {
    "number": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/CheckpointNumber",
      "description": "The checkpoint's number."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "number"
  ],
  "title": "RestoreCheckpointParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `code.actions`

Lists the quick fixes for the diagnostics at a place in a file: a missing builtin declared, a misspelled field corrected, an unused local removed, a missing precache added.

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "ActionIndex": {
```

```json
      "description": "Whether their textures stay fixed in the world; locked when not given."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "entity",
    "brushes",
    "factors"
  ],
  "title": "BrushScaleParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

## `map.brush_shape`

Adds a shape of brushes filling a box, its corners snapped to the grid: a cylinder (solid or hollow), cone, arch, UV or icosahedron spheroid, rock, scalable curve of 12, 24, 48 or 96 sides, or straight or spiral stairs whose default step a player climbs; to the world or an entity of the open map, with a texture.

## `map.brush_shear`

Shears brushes of an entity: each point moves along one axis by a factor times its distance from a point along another, their textures fixed in the world unless lock is free (MAP-15.2).

Parameters:

```json
{
  "$defs": {
    "Axis": {
      "description": "An axis of the world.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "x",
          "description": "x.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "y",
          "description": "y.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "z",
          "description": "z.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "BrushIndex": {
      "description": "A brush, by the entity holding it and its place among that entity's brushes, from 0.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "Lock": {
      "description": "Whether a moved brush's textures stay fixed in the world (P6-09, MAP-11.2).",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "locked",
          "description": "Texture lock on: the textures stay where they are in the world.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "free",
          "description": "Texture lock off: the textures move with the brush.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.brush_shear`.",
  "properties": {
    "about": {
      "default": null,
      "description": "The point kept where it is; the middle of the brushes' bounds when not given.",
      "items": {
        "format": "double",
        "type": "number"
      },
      "maxItems": 3,
      "minItems": 3,
      "type": [
        "array",
        "null"
      ]
    },
    "along": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Axis",
      "description": "The axis points move along."
    },
    "brushes": {
      "description": "The brushes.",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex"
      },
      "type": "array"
    },
    "by": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Axis",
      "description": "The axis their distance from `about` is measured along; another than `along`."
    },
    "entity": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
      "description": "The entity holding the brushes."
    },
    "factor": {
      "description": "How far a point moves along `along` for each unit of that distance.",
      "format": "double",
      "type": "number"
    },
    "lock": {
      "$ref": "#/$defs/Lock",
      "default": "locked",
      "description": "Whether their textures stay fixed in the world; locked when not given."
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "entity",
    "brushes",
    "along",
    "by",
    "factor"
  ],
  "title": "BrushShearParams",
  "type": "object"
}
```

```json
{
  "$defs": {
```

```json
{
  "$defs": {
```

```json
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "EntityIndex": {
      "description": "An entity of a map, by its place in the file from 0, the world first.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "FaceIndex": {
      "description": "A face's place among its brush's faces, from 0, in file order.",
      "format": "uint",
      "minimum": 0,
      "type": "integer"
    },
    "FaceRef": {
      "additionalProperties": false,
      "description": "A face of the open map: the entity, the brush and the face.",
      "properties": {
        "brush": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/BrushIndex",
          "description": "The brush."
        },
        "entity": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/EntityIndex",
          "description": "The entity holding the brush."
        },
        "face": {
          "$ref": "#/$defs/FaceIndex",
          "description": "The face."
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "entity",
        "brush",
        "face"
      ],
      "type": "object"
    },
    "JustifyTo": {
      "description": "Where `justify` puts the texture.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "const": "left",
          "description": "Its left edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "right",
          "description": "Its right edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "top",
          "description": "Its top edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "bottom",
          "description": "Its bottom edge on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        },
        {
          "const": "centre",
          "description": "Its centre on the face's.",
          "type": "string"
        }
      ]
    },
    "UvChoice": {
      "description": "What `map.face_uv` does to each face.",
      "oneOf": [
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,

              "const": "justify",
              "type": "string"
            },
            "to": {
              "$ref": "#/$defs/JustifyTo",

            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind",
            "to"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        },
        {
          "additionalProperties": false,
          "description": "Mirror it along an axis about the face's centre (MAP-13.4).",
          "properties": {

            }
          },

          ],

        },

          },

              },
              "maxItems": 2,
              "minItems": 2,

            }
          },
          "required": [
            "kind"
          ],
          "type": "object"
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "additionalProperties": false,
  "description": "The parameters of `map.face_uv`.",
```

```json
      "type": "object"
    },
    "self_fields": {
      "additionalProperties": true,
      "default": {},
```
